title: Make fixture scanners match semantic role rather than payload text
answer: Rebuilt fixture and content scanners classify a match by parsed JSON field, tool-call verb, or AST node. Historical false positives (8 labelled mentions) produce zero role flags on both scanners; every true-positive invocation still flags. This receipt quotes rm -rf, curl | bash, DROP TABLE, eval(, git push --force, chmod 777 and os.system as examples and is itself classified MENTION. SUCCESS:TST-0341

examples.mention_prose: A fixture that DOCUMENTS rm -rf, curl | bash, DROP TABLE, eval(, git push --force, chmod 777 or os.system necessarily CONTAINS those bytes. Matching payload text flags this receipt and misses nothing real.

historical_false_positives.note: Eight estate hits: markdown fence, JSON description, nested examples[].command, Read payload, Grep search, Python docstring, Python comment, catalog tests_required / question_or_target. Payload text is present in each; the semantic role is MENTION.

tests_required: Historical false-positive corpus -> zero flags after the rebuild.
True-positive corpus -> every real instance still flagged.
Self-reference: this unit's own receipt will contain the forbidden patterns as examples and must not be flagged by the scanner it ships.

evidence.claim: Historical FP corpus is silent under role matching on both scanners; naive substring still fires on every record.
